capabilities: link-shortener | Creates named short links (s/name) for any URL, with tags, private, workspace or public visibility, collections to share several links, and view counts, in a web interface and over an API.
description:
UnitySVC runs the official Slash image in a separate container for each enrollment, with its own HTTPS address. Slash is a self-hosted link shortener and bookmark manager: give any URL a short, readable name such as `s/docs`, tag it, choose who can see it (only you, signed-in users, or anyone), group links into collections you can share, and see how often each link was opened. Everything is kept in the instance's own SQLite database, stored in the `slash` folder of your home, so it survives stopping the instance and even removing it and enrolling again.

Enroll in the base channel; it asks for no settings. Open the instance address and register an account straight away: the first account registered on a new instance becomes its administrator, so anyone who reaches the address before you could take that role. Then turn off user registration in Slash's settings. You can run one Slash instance at a time. See How to use this service for full setup and limitations.

You pay the selected channel's platform compute cost while the instance runs, including idle time, and the platform keeps the data in your home while it is stopped. Labs adds no markup and receives no seller payout. This runs Slash 1.0.0-rc.3, a release candidate, and Slash's own free plan limits an instance to 5 accounts, 100 shortcuts and 5 collections. See the upstream Slash documentation and issue tracker for software-specific help.

features: Short `s/name` links for any URL, with tags and visibility settings
Collections that share several links at once
A view count for each link
Web interface and an HTTP API with access tokens
Your data is kept in your home, across stops, restarts and re-enrollment
